name: hdie_pc_ctrl_cfg_h9c

job.purpose: H9c (HBMA-H9B 2026-10-17): the CLOSED h9b view (route hdie_pc_ctrl_cfg_h9b-h9b-pinflop-ring-7c8e3dc3c, main 119241ed7) FAILS the native audit (results/rtl/hbm_lane_a_1017/native_1017.json, claude/hbma-lane-1017 bfa86913e): capture 213.7 ps > 190 on 352 inputs, TT boundary insertion R 455.4 ps, spread 117.5 ps > 80. The pins are already pin flops (RTL unchanged); the cause is the clock: a pre-placed macro-leaf SPINE over 8,555 sinks across 185.76 x 164.16. H9c: local TritonCTS (a leaf tile with no hard children), outline 155.52 x 155.52 at std density ~0.54 (the d4f SYNTH slot 139.104 x 139.32 would put the 6,327 um2 std area at ~0.61-0.71 of the macro-free core), both SRAMs abutted N-S, pushed to the 20-um E channel (all SRAM pins are on the macro W face) so the W column (~31 um) holds the register mass in one contiguous ring band; pin faces N K/KR, S PHY, W clk/rst_n/owner_fault_split plus the strap/fault pins pc_fault/pc_id/refresh_reload moved from E (gate 2: the E-channel sinks beyond the SRAM stack measured 300-320 ps vs 221-270 elsewhere, boundary spread 95), E face empty, clock entry W beside the register mass, N/S buses spread by the kit over full faces. Pins: the h9b die grants (physical/hbm_die_pins/pc_cfg_h9, cf302625a) rescaled to the new faces with the same order and layers (physical/hbm_die_pins/pc_cfg_h9c/pins.tcl): N 622 / S 585 over the full 146.6 um face, W 22, ~4.2 pins/um.

pin_regs.reason: H9b registers every pin in RTL: every K input lands in a pure pin flop (kp_*, data unconditional), k_rdy is a flop, kr_rdy is pin-registered (kr_rdy_q), KR outputs leave the per-64b skid head flops, PHY commands leave OREG flops, PHY return enters RREG flops, straps enter pc_id_q/refresh_reload_q; a kit flop stage would add a redundant edge
